# UQDA Core v0.1.2

This operations and performance release supersedes v0.1.1. It keeps the v0.1.1
network protocol and group-password derivation, so v0.1.1 nodes can be upgraded
without a coordinated network-wide restart.

## Home and venue gateways

- Adds the `uqda-gateway` command for running one UQDA node as a gateway for
  ordinary phones, tablets, computers, and televisions.
- Supports a NetworkManager profile for Raspberry Pi OS, Debian, and Ubuntu,
  with explicit WAN/Wi-Fi selection, IPv4 Internet sharing, IPv6 SLAAC for the
  node's routed UQDA `/64`, read-only planning, status, and targeted rollback.
- Adds an experimental OpenWrt/UCI profile. OpenWrt routers remain
  model-dependent and must pass the documented hardware acceptance tests
  before production use.
- Adds a hardened café/public-hotspot profile with Wi-Fi client isolation,
  blocked access to the gateway and private upstream networks, explicit
  DHCP/DNS/essential-ICMPv6 allowances, disabled WPS, PMF support, firewall
  persistence, safe activation ordering, and emergency rollback.
- Requires an explicit `--public` acknowledgement before public hotspot mode
  can be applied.

## Latency and diagnostics

- Adds the `uqda-latency` helper, reporting packet loss, minimum, average, p50,
  p95, maximum, and successive-sample jitter.
- Defines the default measurable target as zero loss and p95 RTT at or below
  20 ms, while documenting that distance, ISP routing, Wi-Fi, congestion, and
  remote hosts prevent a universal latency guarantee.
- Adds `uqdactl getPeers sort=latency` (or `sort=rtt`) so measured direct
  peers are listed fastest-first, followed by unknown and down peers.
- Documents nearby/direct peer selection, idle-versus-loaded testing,
  Ethernet/Wi-Fi comparison, and SQM/CAKE bufferbloat diagnosis.

## Installation and documentation

- Adds a project-owned Homebrew Cask installation path for macOS. Homebrew may
  require the scoped `brew trust --cask uqda/core/uqda` command because the
  Cask executes the project's verified installer.
- Expands the English project guide and adds dedicated home gateway, café
  gateway, performance, release, and verification documentation.
- Publishes `uqda-gateway` and `uqda-latency` as checksum-covered release
  assets alongside `install.sh`, platform packages, signed `SHA256SUMS`, and
  provenance attestations.

## macOS notice

The project still does not use a paid Apple Developer account. macOS packages
are explicitly named `*-unsigned.pkg`. Finder may display a Gatekeeper warning.
Use the command-line `install.sh` path or the project Homebrew Cask: the
installer verifies the package against this release's SHA-256 manifest before
invoking the macOS system installer. Do not disable Gatekeeper globally.

## Validation

The release quality gate reruns:

- unit tests, formatting, linting, CodeQL, reachable dependency scanning,
  race-sensitive coverage, and handshake fuzzing;
- deterministic gateway and latency-helper safety tests;
- Linux, Windows, and macOS builds/tests with the supported Go toolchains;
- FreeBSD and OpenBSD cross-builds;
- privileged two-node, multi-hop, failover, loss/latency, and secure-required
  mesh scenarios;
- installer platform selection and native package builds; and
- checksum generation, Sigstore verification, and GitHub provenance
  attestations.

Software tests cannot validate every Wi-Fi chipset, regulatory domain, or
OpenWrt router. Operators must run the documented client-isolation, reboot,
Internet, UQDA reachability, management separation, and rollback checks on the
exact gateway hardware before serving other users.
